title: Pacing at 2 minutes per item and reviewing your answers
blurb: Pace Part A at no more than 2 minutes per item, answer every item, and use spare minutes to check format.
question: Part A has 15 items in 30 minutes and you have answered 9 after 20 minutes. How should you pace the rest?

teach.body: Part A has 15 one-mark items in 30 minutes, and the pass mark is 13 out of 15 (87%) for every field. The NMC booklet advises spending no more than 2 minutes on each numeracy question. There is no negative marking and no partial credit, and you can review and change answers. Plain English: keep moving, answer every item, and use spare minutes to check format.
teach.cite: NMC test specification s6.1.1; NMC CBT booklet (April 2025)

teach.caption: Quick items (unit conversions, pot readings) bank time for review.

steps.label: Stuck at 2 min?
steps.sub: Best answer, note number, move on

teach.h: Worked example: Lena checks the clock
teach.body: Lena, a midwife sitting Part A, has answered 9 items after 20 minutes. Time left = 10 minutes for 6 items: 10 ÷ 6 = 1.67 minutes each. She is slightly behind a 2-minute pace, so she enters a best answer on item 11, notes "11" on her note board and moves on, leaving a minute to return to it.

rows.label: Stuck item
values: Best answer, note it, move on

teach.text: The time sink: one stubborn item eats five minutes and two easy items at the end go unanswered. With a 13/15 pass mark you can afford at most 2 wrong answers, so a blank box is a mark thrown away. Enter your best answer and keep moving.

items: 15 items in 30 minutes: 2 minutes each at most.
Pass = 13/15, so no more than 2 wrong.
No negative marking: answer every item.
Note stuck item numbers on the note board and return.
Use review time for unit, decimal places, zeros and sign.

summary: You can now pace Part A at no more than 2 minutes per item, recheck your pace with minutes left ÷ items left and answer every item. You can also use review time for the format checks that decide marks.

A.q: Part A has 15 items in 30 minutes. On average, how many minutes are available for each item?
A.why: 30 ÷ 15 = 2 minutes per item, which matches the NMC advice of no more than 2 minutes.

A.q: A 15-item numeracy test has a pass mark of 13. What is the largest number of items that can be answered incorrectly while still passing?

whyNot.2: Allowed one fewer wrong answer than the pass mark permits.
whyNot.3: This is the number that must be correct.

A.q: The pass mark for a 15-item numeracy test is 13 correct. What percentage is this? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.3: This is the percentage that can be wrong.

B.q: In a 30-minute numeracy test with 15 items, 20 minutes have passed and 9 items are answered. On average, how many minutes are left for each remaining item? Write your answer to one decimal place.
B.why: Time left = 30 − 20 = 10 minutes. Items left = 15 − 9 = 6. 10 ÷ 6 = 1.666..., so 1.7 minutes.

whyNot.0: Divided by the 9 answered items instead of the 6 left.

B.q: In a 30-minute numeracy test with 15 items, you plan to keep 5 minutes at the end for review. On average, how many minutes can you spend on each item? Write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: Added the review time instead of subtracting it.
whyNot.3: Left out the 5 minutes kept for review.

B.q: The test clock shows 8 minutes 30 seconds remaining and 4 items are unanswered. On average, how many minutes are available for each item? Write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: Treated 30 seconds as 0.3 minutes; it is 0.5 minutes.
whyNot.1: Rounded the final 5 down; half-up rounding gives 2.13.

C.q: A candidate is confident that 11 of her 15 Part A answers are correct and is unsure about the other 4. The pass mark is 13. How many of the 4 unsure answers must be correct for her to pass?

whyNot.0: Assumed every unsure answer must be right.
whyNot.2: One short: 11 + 1 = 12, below the pass mark.

C.q: In a 30-minute, 15-item test you spend 1.5 minutes on each of the first 10 items and 2 minutes on each of the last 5. How many minutes are left for review?
C.why: First 10: 10 × 1.5 = 15 minutes. Last 5: 5 × 2 = 10 minutes. Review = 30 − 15 − 10 = 5 minutes.

whyNot.0: Left out the time spent on the last 5 items.

C.q: After 10 minutes of a 15-item test, a candidate has answered 6 items. If she keeps the same pace, how many minutes will all 15 items take?

whyNot.1: Used 7 items (the one she is on) instead of 6 answered.
whyNot.3: Assumed 2 minutes per item instead of her actual pace.

reteach.title: Minutes left ÷ items left
reteach.question: With 12 minutes left and 6 items to go, how long per item?

blocks.body: Minutes left ÷ items left = time per item. 12 ÷ 6 = 2 minutes: on pace. If the answer drops well below 2, speed up on quick items and note any stuck item to return to.

blocks.text: Dividing by the items already answered instead of the items left gives a falsely comfortable pace.

explain.body: Answering time ÷ 15 items = average time per item.

test.q: You plan to spend 24 minutes answering the 15 items and keep the rest for review. On average, how many minutes is that per item? Write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.2: Used 30 minutes instead of the 24 planned.

explain.body: 13 of 15 must be correct, so 2 can be wrong.

test.q: A 15-item test has a pass mark of 13. What percentage of the items can be answered incorrectly while still passing? Write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: This is the pass percentage, not the wrong percentage.
whyNot.2: Gave the number of items, not the percentage.

explain.body: Recheck your pace at each third of the paper.

test.q: The clock shows 11 minutes left and 6 items are unanswered. On average, how many minutes are available for each item? Write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.2: Rounded 1.83 up; the next digit is 3.

explain.body: Review time = time left − time needed for the remaining items.

test.q: You have 7 minutes left and 4 items to answer. If each takes 1.25 minutes, how many minutes will be left for review?

whyNot.0: Allowed for one item instead of four.
whyNot.1: This is the time the 4 items take.
whyNot.3: Allowed 1 minute per item instead of 1.25.
